correctness.rationale: For every compact planar convex K, the multiplicity-corrected boundary measure has mass <=2*pi*r in an origin-centered ball of radius r: by convex perimeter inclusion for K intersect the disk, or double-length for a segment. The support-function first-variation formula is reconstructed explicitly, with the tangential derivative canceled by integration by parts. For -1<p<0, truncation f_e=min(r^p,e^p) gives gradient bound 2*pi*(1-p)*e^p and total two-set cutoff error 4*pi*(-p)*e^(p+1)/(p+1); choosing e=d_H yields the claimed C_p. For p>=0 the gradient integral gives the R^p bound and the p=0 sharp coefficient. Smooth-approximation passage holds for all convex sets by local mass control and weak convergence of multiplicity-corrected boundary measures. Point/disk and nearby concentric disks prove the optimal exponents. The standalone finite-check script was executed successfully; no numerical test is mistaken for an all-set proof.

value.rationale: Singular origin-centered geometric surface energies arise naturally in 2026 convex-body weighted-perimeter optimization. Determining a global modulus without diameter dependence, showing an exact sharp exponent p+1 for all -1<p<0, and locating the transition to Lipschitz at p=0 resolve a natural quantitative stability gap left by qualitative continuity. The sharp degeneration examples and full class of convex sets make this a structural sharp regularity law, not an arbitrary finite exercise. The prefactors outside p=0 are not claimed optimal.
